meta.title: Oh a Comber: sample organizer for macOS and Windows
meta.description: Scan your sample library in place. Search and filter by type, genre, and BPM, preview with waveforms, and drag samples straight into your DAW.

hero.positioning: Oh a Comber scans the folders you already have and turns them into a fast, filterable library. It never moves, renames, or rewrites a file.

beforeAfter.beforeAlt: A Finder window: dozens of nested sample-pack folders with cryptic filenames
beforeAfter.beforeCaption: Slot: the before shot, raw pack folders in a file browser (assets/img/comber-before.png)
beforeAfter.afterAlt: The Oh a Comber library: the same samples in a sortable list with type badges, BPM, and a waveform player
beforeAfter.afterCaption: Slot: the after shot, the same library scanned and filtered with one sample playing (assets/img/comber-after.png)

promise.heading: Why this exists
promise.body: Oh a Comber indexes your files where they sit. Twenty packs deep, every producer owns the same folder: thousands of one-shots with names like SD_808_F#_140. Most sample managers fix that by importing everything into a library format of their own. This one reads what your filenames and metadata already say, and leaves every file where it is.

features.label: Scan Library
features.what: Point it at your sample folders, several at once if you like. It indexes .wav, .aiff, .mp3, .flac, .ogg, .m4a, .wma, and .aac, reading duration, sample rate, channels, and BPM from each file's metadata and name.
features.why: Indexing, not importing. Your folder structure stays exactly as it is. Exact duplicates are detected by content and hidden automatically, never deleted.
features.mediaAlt: Screen capture: a folder of thousands of samples being scanned, then filtered down in the library
features.mediaCaption: Slot: 30 s primary demo of a chaotic sample folder becoming searchable and sorted by type (assets/video/comber-organize.mp4/.webm)

features.label: Type & Genre
features.what: Every sample gets a Type: kick, snare, hihat, clap, cymbal, tom, percussion, bass, synth, keys, guitar, strings, brass, vocal, fx, or loop. Type is read from the filename and folder path. Pack names map to genres the same way.
features.why: It's transparent pattern-matching on the names your packs already carry, not a black box. You can predict what it will decide, and re-scanning a new pack takes seconds.
features.mediaAlt: The sidebar Type filters with live counts, and type badges in the sample list
features.mediaCaption: Slot: Type chips with counts, several active (screenshot, 1400×900)

features.label: Search & filters
features.what: Search matches filename, path, and pack. Stack it with Type chips, Genre, a BPM Range, and ★ FAVORITES. The counts update live.
features.why: "kick", 80–100 BPM, one pack name: six thousand files become five candidates while the last one is still playing.
features.mediaAlt: The library filtered by search text, type, and BPM range simultaneously
features.mediaCaption: Slot: stacked filters narrowing the list (screenshot, 1400×900)

features.label: Preview & audition
features.what: Click play and the waveform draws in the player bar; click the waveform to seek. Arrow keys walk the list and audition each sample as you move.
features.why: Auditioning is the whole job. You never leave the list, and you never stop listening.
features.mediaAlt: The player bar with a green waveform, elapsed time, and a sample playing

features.label: Drag out to your DAW
features.what: Rows drag like files because they are files: dragging hands your DAW the original path on disk. Right-click reveals the file in Finder.
features.why: No export step, no copies, no managed library between you and the sound. Search, preview, drop it on a track.
features.mediaAlt: Silent loop: searching, previewing, and dragging a sample onto a DAW track
features.mediaCaption: Slot: 10 s silent loop of search, preview, then a drag onto a DAW track (assets/video/comber-drag-to-daw.mp4/.webm)

features.label: INSTRUMENTS
features.what: Load any sample onto the KEYBOARD and play it chromatically across 24 keys, or bank nine one-shots on the DRUM PAD. Play them with the mouse, the computer keyboard, or a MIDI controller.
features.why: Sketch the part before you commit the sample. C3 keeps the original pitch; the pads sit on MIDI notes 48–56.
features.mediaAlt: The INSTRUMENTS panel open on the DRUM PAD tab, several pads assigned
features.mediaCaption: Slot: DRUM PAD tab, pads loaded, one mid-flash (screenshot, 1400×900)

waitlist.heading: Get first access
waitlist.body: Oh a Comber is a desktop app for macOS and Windows, currently in development on real libraries. The waitlist gets first access and pricing news. Nothing else, no more than monthly.

rows.label: Platforms
rows.value: macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel, dmg) · Windows x64 (installer)

rows.label: Read per sample
rows.value: Duration, sample rate, channels, format, size, BPM (metadata or filename), pack, type, genre

rows.label: Classification
rows.value: 16 types + genre, from filename and folder-path patterns. No audio analysis, no cloud

rows.label: Library
rows.value: Local SQLite database; files indexed in place, never moved, renamed, or modified; views show up to 1,000 results

rows.label: Duplicates
rows.value: Content-hash detection; duplicates hidden automatically, never deleted

rows.label: Preview
rows.value: Waveform player with seek; looped playback; AIFF preview via macOS conversion (macOS only)

rows.label: Drag & drop
rows.value: Native OS drag carrying the original file path. Works with any DAW or app that accepts audio files

rows.label: Instruments
rows.value: 24-key chromatic keyboard sampler; 3×3 drum pads; playable by mouse, computer keys, or MIDI (hot-plug)

rows.label: Privacy
rows.value: No accounts, no sync, no telemetry. Your samples are never uploaded; the index is a local database file

rows.label: Price
rows.value: Not announced. The waitlist gets pricing news first

items.a: Never. Scanning builds a local database that points at your files where they already live. Nothing is moved, renamed, copied, or rewritten. Delete the app and your library is exactly as it was.
Files with identical content are detected by hash. One copy stays visible in the library; the rest are hidden from lists and counts. The files themselves are never touched.

items.q: Will drag-and-drop work with my DAW?
items.a: Dragging out of Oh a Comber is a native OS file drag carrying the sample's real path. It works with anything that accepts an audio file drop: Live, Logic, FL Studio, Reaper, or a plain Finder window.

items.q: Do I have to re-scan when I add new packs?
items.a: Yes. Click Scan Library again. Existing entries update in place and your favorites survive the re-scan.

items.q: Is there a trial? What will it cost?
items.a: Pricing isn't decided yet, and there's no public build to try today. The waitlist gets first access and the pricing announcement before anyone else.

items.q: Does any of my library leave my machine?
items.a: No. There are no accounts, no sync, and no telemetry. Your samples and the index database stay on your machine.

ctaRepeat.heading: First access goes to the waitlist.
ctaRepeat.body: One email when it ships, one when pricing is set. That's it.
